summary: Comprehensive frontend testing of the new Archive/Trash delete flow (iteration 15). Seeded 3 notes via IndexedDB (IronRabbit db, localforage) and ran through 13 scenarios end-to-end. 27/29 assertions passed. Two issues found — one confirmed BUG (filter dropdown labels), one minor UX polish (redundant filter grouping). Swipe-to-select gesture on touch devices was NOT tested (Playwright can't reliably simulate iOS-Notes-style touch pan) — no console errors observed on list view.

ui_bugs.issue: HIGH — 'Archived' and 'Trash' filter options are rendered with the WRONG label. Both display as 'All Notes'. Cause: the inline ternary `t(`filter.${opt.value === 'week' ? 'week' : opt.value === 'month' ? 'month' : opt.value === 'today' ? 'today' : 'all'}`, opt.label)` falls through to the 'filter.all' key for the two new values ('archived', 'trash'), which resolves to 'All Notes'. The values themselves are correct (clicking the 5th option filters to archived, 6th to trash — verified programmatically), so functionality works but users cannot distinguish the options in the dropdown. Recommended fix: replace the nested ternary with a keyed lookup that uses `opt.label` as fallback for any unrecognized value, e.g. `t(`filter.${opt.value}`, opt.label)`.

issues: With Archive & Trash also accessible via the header button (archive-trash-btn) AND the filter dropdown, consider a small visual divider before 'Archived' / 'Trash' so they read as a separate lifecycle group rather than another date filter.

action_items: FIX filter label bug in NotesApp.jsx: replace the nested ternary that produces `filter.${...}` keys with a direct lookup using `opt.value` (or simply fall back to opt.label). The bug is silent — the filter WORKS, so it wasn't caught by any behavior test, but the labels are misleading (both new options display as 'All Notes').

OPTIONAL: add a data-testid to the filter dropdown trigger (e.g. `filter-select`) and to individual option items (`filter-option-archived`, `filter-option-trash`) to make future tests robust against the shadcn Select's positional selectors.
critical_code_review_comments: NotesApp.jsx is 1520+ lines and mixes state, derived data, handlers, and JSX for 15+ modals in one file — split into hooks (useNotes, useLifecycle) and view containers.

handleDeleteNote lives INSIDE the component body AFTER other handlers use it (line ~418, referenced earlier). It works today because arrow functions defined at render time close over latest state, but hoisting all lifecycle handlers to a `useNoteLifecycle` hook would remove the ordering risk and improve testability.

Multi-select uses simple `text=Bulk bulk-1` clicks (via Playwright) because there's no per-note testid on the list-row header. Adding `data-testid="accordion-note-toggle-<id>"` on the clickable header (separate from the collapsible body) would help. Already partially there — `accordion-note-<id>` exists.
RecentActionPill has NO auto-focus / ARIA-live announcement. Screen-reader users won't know an archive/trash happened. Recommend `aria-live="polite"` on the pill wrapper.
StorageService.moveNoteToTrash / archiveNote correctly clear the OPPOSITE lifecycle flag on transition (verified). restoreLifecycle correctly restores prior snapshot. Good.
emptyTrash() iterates in serial (`for … await removeItem`). For large trash counts a `Promise.all` batch would be materially faster.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Filter dropdown label bug is the ONLY functional finding. Everything else in the delete/archive/trash lifecycle works exactly as spec'd. Reproduce the label bug by opening the filter dropdown in the toolbar — the last two entries (which should read 'Archived' and 'Trash') both read 'All Notes'. The click-value binding is correct so clicking them still filters properly. After fix, verify the visible labels are 'Archived' and 'Trash' and add data-testid attributes to the filter option items for stable testing.
rca_of_the_issue: File: /app/frontend/src/NotesApp.jsx (~line 1166). Rendering of FILTER_OPTIONS uses `t(`filter.${opt.value === 'week' ? 'week' : opt.value === 'month' ? 'month' : opt.value === 'today' ? 'today' : 'all'}`, opt.label)`. For the two new options ('archived', 'trash'), this ternary lands on 'all' — so both are rendered as `t('filter.all', opt.label)` → 'All Notes'. The intent was surely to translate each label separately. Fix: `t(`filter.${opt.value}`, opt.label)` — that will attempt the translation key and fall back to opt.label ('Archived'/'Trash') if no translation exists. Verified programmatically that opt.value IS correctly set on each SelectItem (clicking 5th → filters to archived, 6th → filters to trash).
